subject: anatomy
title: Inguinal Canal Architecture: Deep Ring, Spermatic Cord, and Hernia Triangles

steps.tx: The proximal entrance to the inguinal canal is the **deep inguinal ring**, an oval opening in the endoabdominal fascia transversalis located 1.25 centimetres superior to the midinguinal point (midway between the ASIS and pubic symphysis). The inferior epigastric artery ascends immediately medial to the medial margin of this ring.
steps.say: The entrance to the inguinal canal is the deep inguinal ring, an aperture in fascia transversalis above the midinguinal point. The inferior epigastric artery ascends immediately medial to this ring.

vis.alt: Posterior view of the groin showing the deep inguinal ring and Hesselbach triangle
vis.caption: Posterior view of groin anatomy illustrating the deep inguinal ring and inferior epigastric vessels. [Credit: Dennis M. DePace, PhD / Wikimedia Commons]

steps.tx: Traversing the inguinal canal in males is the **spermatic cord**, extending from the deep ring through the superficial ring into the scrotum. It comprises three arteries, three nerves, and three other structures, all enveloped by three concentric fascial coverings acquired as it evaginates the layers of the abdominal wall.
steps.say: The spermatic cord passes through the inguinal canal into the scrotum. It contains three arteries, three nerves, and three other structures, wrapped in three concentric fascial coats derived from the abdominal wall.

rows: External oblique aponeurosis at superficial ring

steps.tx: The contents of the spermatic cord follow the rule of threes: three arteries (testicular artery, artery to vas deferens, and cremasteric artery); three nerves (genital branch of genitofemoral, sympathetic autonomic fibres, and ilioinguinal nerve on the cord exterior); and three other structures: the **vas deferens**, pampiniform venous plexus, and lymphatics.
steps.say: Spermatic cord contents follow the rule of threes: three arteries, three nerves, and three other structures: the vas deferens, pampiniform venous plexus, and testicular lymphatics.

rows: Supplies cremaster muscle and cord coats

steps.tx: An **indirect inguinal hernia** enters the deep inguinal ring lateral to the inferior epigastric vessels, traveling the entire length of the inguinal canal within the coverings of the spermatic cord toward the scrotum. In children and young adults, it results from patency of the embryonic processus vaginalis.
steps.say: An indirect inguinal hernia enters the deep ring lateral to the inferior epigastric vessels, traversing the full length of the canal inside the cord. It arises from a persistent patent processus vaginalis.

vis.alt: Formalin-fixed specimen jar containing an excised indirect inguinal hernial sac
vis.caption: Surgically excised indirect inguinal hernial sac demonstrating fibrous peritoneal composition. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: The medial inguinal triangle of **Hesselbach** defines the site of direct inguinal herniation. Its boundaries comprise: laterally the inferior epigastric artery, medially the lateral border of the rectus abdominis muscle (linea semilunaris), and inferiorly the medial half of the inguinal ligament.
steps.say: Hesselbach triangle marks the site where direct inguinal hernias push through. Its borders are the inferior epigastric artery laterally, rectus abdominis medially, and inguinal ligament inferiorly.

left.title: Hesselbach Triangle Boundaries
points: Medial: Lateral border of rectus abdominis

right.title: Surgical Division of Triangle
points: Medial umbilical fold divides triangle into two fossae
Medial fossa: direct hernia emerges through conjoint gap
Lateral fossa: direct hernia pushes through transversalis
Always medial to inferior epigastric vessels

steps.tx: A **direct inguinal hernia** protrudes directly forward through the attenuated floor of Hesselbach triangle, medial to the inferior epigastric vessels. Common in elderly men with chronic coughing, benign prostatic hyperplasia, or abdominal wall laxity, it pushes past the conjoint tendon and rarely descends into the scrotum.
steps.say: A direct inguinal hernia pushes straight through the floor of Hesselbach triangle, medial to the inferior epigastric vessels. Prevalent in elderly men with abdominal muscle laxity, it rarely enters the scrotum.

rows: Inferior and lateral to pubic tubercle

steps.tx: Bedside differentiation relies on the **internal ring occlusion test**. The examiner reduces the hernia and applies firm digital pressure over the deep inguinal ring (1.25 cm above midinguinal point). On coughing, an indirect hernia is completely prevented from appearing, whereas a direct hernia continues to bulge forward medial to the occluding finger.
steps.say: The internal ring occlusion test differentiates groin hernias. By pressing over the deep ring, coughing will not produce an indirect hernia, while a direct hernia continues to bulge forward medial to the finger.

nodes.label: Completely Reduce Groin Hernial Swelling while Patient Supine
Place Finger Firmly 1.25 cm Above Midinguinal Point
Ask Patient to Cough or Perform Valsalva Maneuver
Controlled: Indirect Hernia; Uncontrolled Medial Bulge: Direct Hernia

steps.tx: Surgical hernia repair must respect the triangle of doom and **triangle of pain** seen during laparoscopic totally extraperitoneal (TEP) or transabdominal preperitoneal (TAPP) repair. The triangle of doom is bounded by the vas deferens medially and gonadal vessels laterally, containing the external iliac artery and vein where tacking staples are strictly forbidden.
steps.say: Laparoscopic hernia repairs must avoid the triangle of doom and triangle of pain. The triangle of doom contains external iliac vessels between vas and gonadal vessels where staples must never be placed.

left.title: Triangle of Doom (Vascular)
points: Bounded by vas deferens and spermatic vessels
Contains external iliac artery and vein
Stapling here causes fatal arterial hemorrhage

right.title: Triangle of Pain (Neural)
points: Bounded by gonadal vessels and iliopubic tract
Contains lateral femoral cutaneous and femoral nerves
Stapling here produces chronic neuropathic inguinodynia
